question: Can the NLC-linked digital object FID 412004000070 be durably crosswalked to the 1985 NLC microfilm old-catalog description of a 32-book Yuan copy repaired in Ming, and does that prove identity with Zhang Lijuan's Tieqin-old-collection Yuan-impression witness?
answer: The digital/microfilm/old-catalog crosswalk is closed, but exact Tieqin physical identity remains strongly compatible rather than proved. Two independent 1985 NLC microfilm records for 《附释音春秋左传注疏》 directly embed 455$1 original-record control 001412004000070 and describe the original as a 32-book rare printed copy, Yuan [1271-1368], repaired in Ming [1368-1644]. The work/master-style record is SYS 003416361 / UID UCS01003624709 and carries microfilm registration/login number 905$b 00O003551; the distribution-copy record is SYS 003026493 / UID UCS01003601976. A Wikimedia Commons library-backup index with National Library of China attribution independently exposes FID 412004000070 as exactly 32 PDF books covering juan 1 through 60. This closes FID 412004000070 as the digitized original referenced by the 1985 NLC microfilm old-catalog layer. Zhang Lijuan's official NOPSS project report says the NLC Tieqin Tongjian Lou old-collection ten-line copy was formerly cataloged as '元刻明修本' and was re-adjudicated by physical examination as '元刻元印十行本'. The wording and object profile are therefore strongly compatible with the FID-070 object, but the reviewed evidence still lacks an explicit Tieqin ownership/provenance note, modern NLC shelfmark/905s, accession crosswalk, or unique seal/defect fingerprint tying FID 070 to Zhang's physical copy. Same-object identity is therefore not promoted beyond STRONGLY_COMPATIBLE_NOT_PROVED.
